title: Coffee Order
story: You work at a hipster coffee shop. Every order has a size (S/M/L), a milk choice (none, regular, oat, almond), and a number of espresso shots. The register needs to compute the price based on all three choices — a large oat milk latte with 3 shots costs more than a small black coffee.
why: Combining two enums with a struct and a price method demonstrates real-world business logic.
analogy: A coffee order is like building a custom sandwich. Size is footlong or 6-inch. Milk is cheese type (none/cheddar/swiss/vegan). Shots are extra meat portions. The price method is the cashier scanning each add-on and punching it into the register.
try_it: Add a `WhippedCream: Bool` field to Coffee that adds $0.75. Add decaf option (enum). Add a loyalty discount: if this is the 10th coffee, subtract $2.00. Create your actual coffee order.
tips: Build price incrementally: start with the base, then add each modifier one at a time
Use `!=` to check for "not none" — `milk != Milk.None` means any milk type adds a charge
Extra shots beyond 2 cost money: `(shots - 2) as Float64 * 0.75`
common_mistakes: Forgetting to cast `(shots - 2)` to Float64 before multiplying by 0.75
Charging for extra shots even when shots <= 2 — use `if shots > 2` to guard the surcharge
